sources.title: Act 200 of 2002, South Carolina Conservation Bank Act, Section 5 (suspension of deed-fee transfers)
sources.quote: In a fiscal year when the General Assembly in the annual general appropriations act provides less appropriations than what was provided for the previous year to at least one-half of the state agencies or departments contained therein the act or in any year when the Budget and Control Board orders across the board cuts to state agencies and departments in the manner provided by law, no further transfer of deed recording fees or other appropriated funds, state or local, may be credited to the trust fund for the fiscal year or balance of the fiscal year
sources.note: Quoted in S.139 of 2011-2012, the bill that proposed deleting this section.

sources.title: Review of the South Carolina Conservation Bank's Accounting Practices and Grant Funding Procedures, Case #2017-2554-I
sources.publisher: South Carolina Office of the State Inspector General
sources.quote: In FY 2018, the Bank's funding from the state deed recording fee was suspended in accordance with Proviso 53.1.

sources.title: S. 139, S.C. Conservation Bank Reauthorization and Stabilization Act (2011-2012)
sources.note: Proposed deleting the Act 200 Section 5 suspension trigger and the sunset provision.

sources.title: S.C. Code of Laws Section 12-24-95, deed recording fee allocation
